name: mirage
text: Not tax advice, and I'm assuming US. Short version: yes, it can matter even though you're about even. Gambling winnings are taxable income, and the IRS looks at winnings and losses separately, not your net. 1) The income is your profit on winning bets (payout minus the stake you got back), not the whole $5000 of payouts if that figure includes returned stakes. 2) You report it on Schedule 1 as other income. 3) Losses only offset it if you itemize deductions (Schedule A), and only up to the amount of winnings. Under the 2025 tax law, from the 2026 tax year only 90% of losses are deductible, so a break-even year can still leave a small taxable amount. If you take the standard deduction, you owe tax on the full winnings with no loss offset. 4) Hard part is records: keep Novig's full bet history and the app's Tracker export for every bet with date, stake and result; the winning-bets total and the losing-bets total are the two numbers you need. A tax preparer can do this in a few minutes if you hand them those two totals. Whether itemizing beats the standard deduction for you is the thing to ask them.
